shortName: University of California, Los Angeles David Geffen School of Medicine
additionalCoursework: Awareness of healthcare delivery, health equity, community, and research are recommended.  Attainment of skills in writing and communications, clinical experiences, and interpersonal skills are recommended. In-person courses are strongly recommended for science coursework.

medSchoolStudLife.diversity: We pride ourselves on the diversity of our student body. Multiple programs to celebrate our diverse community and are part of student life and integral to the learning environment.  DGSOM and UCLA health are committed to inclusive excellence and we have developed innovative programs, which promote and train a diverse community of physicians. These programs include: combating structural racism, antiracism roadmap, the gender health program, and health equity, and translational social science research program.
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: Students are provided Leaves of Absence as needed and approved by the Associate Dean of Student Affairs. Leaves are granted for Personal, Medical, Research and Academic reasons.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: Student wellness and life is very important for success in the curriculum and as future physicians.  We have a very robust student body that is active in numerous student organizations and activities.  These include a number of Career Student Interest Groups, national and local student organizations.  Students work both with the Student Affairs Office and the Student Government in coordinating these groups as well as providing resources and funding.   The School of Medicine is located on the UCLA campus so athletics are part of the resources available through intramural groups as well as the Wooden athletic center, etc.
medSchoolStudLife.setting: We are located on the main UCLA campus offering numerous opportunities for theater, recreation, athletics and cultural events.   This and the location of the campus on the west side of Los Angeles make UCLA an ideal place to study, learn and explore.
medSchoolStudLife.housing: Graduate housing is available a short distance from campus.  Married student housing is available in a location close to the campus.  Apartments close to the school and in proximate location to the affiliated hospitals are also available.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems: The David Geffen School of Medicine offers an active Pride Alliance focused on a strong school-wide community that supports LGBTQ+ individuals and can meet the health needs of LGBTQ+ patients with compassionate and competent care.  Pride Alliance is a support network for UCLA medical students, residents and faculty who identify as gay, lesbian, bisexual, transgender, intersex, queer, asexual, two-spirit, questioning, and allies.  In addition to providing networking for students, staff, and faculty, the alliance also provides service in the community and advocacy for change. The UCLA LGBTQ Campus Resource Center also provides counseling, networking, education, and advocacy.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystemsForDisabilities: DGSOM offers resources and services to medical students through our Center for Accessible education, including individual appointments and learning support services.
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms: DGSOM is dedicated to helping students maintain balance, manage stress, and have social wellness during medical school. Please see our website for more details: https://medschool.ucla.edu/education/md-education/student-life-and-events/well-being
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture: The Cultural North Star is our guiding school-wide initiative that embodies who we are and why we're here--Do What's Right. Make Things Better. Be Kind.--We believe that a strong organizational culture is critical to our ability to achieve our mission and vital to our well-being and cohesion as a community. The Cultural North Star helps us build and maintain an inclusive, mission-driven culture by mapping our decisions, actions, and interactions to a shared framework.
medSchoolStudLife.transportationAdditionalInfo: DGSOM offers diverse clinical training at sites across the Los Angeles region. Personal transportation is recommended to facilitate student participation in these educational experiences.

medSchoolCurriculum.dressCode: Professional attire with white coats preferred
medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: A Learning Specialist staff is employed full time in Student Affairs.  The staff works with the Course Chairs to provide tutoring for any student who requests it or has any problems with coursework.
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: Central to the first year is the Early Authentic Clinical Experience which is designed to immerse learners in healthcare and includes reflection to cultivate professional identity formation.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: A combination of styles are utilized with emphasis on small group, large group, and case-based learning.
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: Clinical rotations are supported through our affiliated hospitals and medical centers.
medSchoolCurriculum.prematriculationProgram: A formal pre-matriculation program is offered for PrimeLA track and MSTP track students.
medSchoolCurriculum.lectureAttendance: Attendance is required in-person for all elements of the curriculum.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights: After an orientation course called Basecamp, the first 1.5 years includes “Boards & Wards” preparation providing students with foundational medical knowledge in affective, cognitive, and psychomotor domains. USMLE Step 1 study and testing time are in Fall of Year 2. Starting in January of year 2, students rotate through 8 core clerkships including Emergency Medicine, Family Medicine, Internal Medicine, Neurology, OB/GYN, Pediatrics, Psychiatry, and Surgery. Following a year of clerkships, students begin their Discovery experience where they have time reserved for research projects. In year 4, students participate in advanced clinical electives and end the year with a capstone course where groups receive specialty-based instruction and assessment on their clinical skills to prepare for a successful transition to residency. Students receive career guidance and mentorship throughout the curriculum.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: DGSOM is proud of its strong commitment to community health and dedication to our local communities.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms: DGSOM takes pride in research activities for medical students. DGSOM Discovery is a required MD curricular component providing third-year medical students with nearly a year of protected time for substantive experience in an area of interest for the acquisition of attitudes and skills to foster self-directed, lifelong learning and scholarship. DGSOM Discovery experience offers participation in the DGSOM Discovery Area of Concentration (AoC) Program. DGSOM offers eight AoC:  (1) Basic, Clinical, & Translational Research, (2) Global Health, (3) Social Science & Medical Humanities, (4) Innovation & Entrepreneurship, (5) Health Justice & Advocacy, (6) Bioinformatics & Data Science, (7) Medical Education & Leadership, and (8) Health Delivery Improvement Science. Students begin exploration and preparation activities during the first and second year of medical school, with core Discovery activities taking place in the third year.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation: The mission of the medical education program of the David Geffen School of Medicine at UCLA is to prepare graduates for distinguished careers in clinical practice, teaching, research, and public service. Recognizing that medical school is but one phase in a physician's education, the faculty has worked to create an environment where students prepare for a future in which scientific knowledge, societal values, and human needs are ever changing. To meet this challenge, our graduates have the skills to provide quality care for their patients, to contribute to the growth of scientific knowledge, and to continue learning throughout their careers. They are involved in service to the community and demonstrate a firm commitment to the humanistic, ethical, legal and cultural aspects of medicine. We believe that patient-centered care is an integral part of medical education.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement:
We are a groundbreaking community of problem solvers, caregivers, innovators, and lifelong learners with a noble mission—to heal humankind by delivering leading-edge research, education, patient care, and community engagement. 

We represent a diverse and collaborative community of innovators, educators, healthcare providers, and life-long learners who are also committed to 

o	Create world leaders in health and science
o	Discover the basis for health and cures for disease
o	Optimize health through community partnerships
o	Heal humankind one patient at a time

medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo:
**Response to COVID-19 - Information for 2026-2027 Admissions Cycle**

The David Geffen School of Medicine is sensitive to the challenges imposed on applicants due to the COVID-19 pandemic and has taken steps to assess pandemic impact in the mission-aligned holistic application review process. We understand that applicant premedical experiences in the pandemic underwent modifications. There will be various opportunities in the application to detail any impacts on coursework, activities, and beyond. Please note that:

1) Applicants should include all relevant experiences on the application, including virtual or in-person activities.

2) Applicants should include courses whether virtual or in-person. Grading options will be accepted (letter grades or pass/fail assessments) based on personal needs during the years 2020 and 2021.

3) MCAT scores from January, 2022 through September 15, 2026 will be accepted for consideration.

The wide-ranging effects of the pandemic have engendered remarkable resilience in our applicants. We view this resilience as an asset to the field of medicine and the next generation of physicians. Careful consideration of the pandemic will be assessed during the review of in each application.

medSchoolApplication.technicalStandardInfo: At DGSOM, our foremost responsibility is to ensure the safety and well‑being of the patients we serve. Because our mission is to prepare future physicians who are both highly competent and deeply compassionate, all medical students must possess the abilities and attributes essential for completing the MD curriculum and for progressing into residency training. These Technical Non‑Academic Standards outline the fundamental skills, behaviors, and professional qualities that every DGSOM student must meet in order to fulfill the requirements for medical licensure and to uphold the integrity of the medical profession.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid: Dedicated Financial Management / Aid services are integrated within the School of Medicine. Professional DGSOM financial aid counselors provide services for medical students and continue their relationship with students into residency and fellowships. Virtual appointments are provided five days a week.  Our students graduate with low student indebtedness compared to other public and private institutions in the United States.
medSchoolFinancial.tuitionPolicy: Tuition is set by the University of California.  We are on a semester system with partial refund of tuition if a student needs to take a leave prior to the completion of the semester

medSchoolTimeline.eventDetail: Primary application submission - Please submit your application as early as possible to ensure appropriate time for the holistic application review process.  The application deadline is October 1, 2025.

Acceptance offer -  Prior to April 30, you may consider our offer for up to, but not longer than, 15 business days.  The offer must be accepted or declined via the Applicant portal and in the AMCAS Choose Your Medical School tool once it launches in February.  After April 30, 5 business days will be provided for consideration of new offers only.

Plan to Enroll - On or before April 30, 2026, choose the school or program to which you plan to enroll and promptly withdraw your acceptances from all other schools or programs via the AMCAS Choose Your Medical School tool.

Commit to Enroll Deadline MSTP (MD/PhD) - If choosing to enroll with DGSOM MSTP track, by May 8, 2026 at 5:00pm Pacific Time, indicate your intent to matriculate with DGSOM by selecting "Commit to Enroll" with DGSOM using the AMCAS Choose Your Medical School tool.

Commit to Enroll Deadline Traditional MD track and Prime-LA MD track - If choosing to enroll with Traditional MD or Prime-LA Tracks, by June 1, 2026 at 3:00pm Pacific Time, indicate your intent to matriculate with DGSOM by selecting "Commit to Enroll" with DGSOM using the AMCAS Choose Your Medical School tool.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec:
COMPETENCIES
A successful DGSOM at UCLA applicant will have demonstrated attainment of knowledge and/or skills in the following domains:
•	Biological Sciences and Physiology: Cellular and Molecular Biology and Genetics
•	Chemistry, Biochemistry, and Physical Sciences: Inorganic and Organic chemistry, Biochemistry of intermediary metabolism, and associated laboratory activities
•	Humanities: This might include literature and/or art, history, philosophy, religion, ethics, economics, social behavior, psychology
•	Mathematics and Statistics: This might include biomathematics, computer science, matrix algebra
•	Writing and communication skills
•	Clinical Experiences: We value a sustained interest and commitment to medicine.
•	Interpersonal Skills
•	Health care delivery: This could include courses and/or experiences that deal with the ethical, legal, political, public health, scientific and moral challenges facing health care and health care delivery.
•	Human Diversity
•	Research experience
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: Preference is given to applicants with strong academic preparation, broad educational and growth experiences, and evidence of high achievement. Competitive candidates also demonstrate professionalism, integrity, empathy, and a commitment to delivering high‑quality, patient‑centered care. The admissions process is mission-aligned, holistic and includes review of coursework, extracurricular involvement, leadership, community service, and research. Applications are evaluated for indicators of maturity, intellectual ability, cultural awareness, and dedication to serving all patient populations. Final decisions are based on individual qualifications and are made without regard to race, ethnicity, sex, age, sexual orientation, national origin, or disability.
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: The DGSOM recommends that applicants pursue appropriate experience for a career in medicine. Shadowing is one method of obtaining this exposure, but it is not the only accepted method. Applicants are encouraged to explore alternative opportunities. These could include volunteer service in a clinical setting, EMT, scribe, clinical research, CNA, or MA.
